title: Forecast-guided memory hedging for continuous batching
creator: Priya Narayanan
body:
Problem:
Continuous batching and aggressive KV caching have improved throughput and cost, but they increase volatility in GPU memory usage across weights, KV cache, and per-request activations. Sudden bursty arrivals or multi-tenant mixing can push a device past safe headroom, triggering expensive evictions or model degradation. Existing soft-watermarks and reserve ledgers are reactive and tuned for static targets; we need a predictive hedging layer that reserves probabilistic headroom without sacrificing utilization.

Goal:
Design and implement a forecast-guided memory hedging component that: (1) ingests short-term workload forecasts and tail quantile estimates, (2) computes a per-GPU probabilistic reserve ("memory hedge") split across weights/KV/activations, (3) exposes advisory signals to the scheduler and autoscaler to steer batching and routing, and (4) falls back gracefully to eviction/variant routing when needed. The hedge should reduce out-of-memory events by >= 80% on bursty traces while keeping average memory utilization drop < 6%.

Design overview:
- Input signals: moving-window request rate, observed batch size distribution, KV hit/miss ratio, per-tenant priority, current KV footprint, and recent activation sizes.
- Forecast engine: lightweight quantile forecaster (exponentially weighted quantile sketch) predicting 50/90/99th quantiles for per-GPU peak working set over a 30s horizon. Tunable lookahead.
- Hedge computation: convert quantile predictions into a memory reserve using configurable confidence multiplier and a risk budget per GPU. Reserve is represented as three buckets: immutable weights buffer (non-movable), hedged KV headroom, and transient activation cushion.
- Allocation policy: use proportional scaling to split hedge across tenants by priority and estimated KV residency. If predicted headroom deficit > threshold, trigger preemptive throttling of batch coalescing for best-effort traffic and raise autoscaler hints to provision burst capacity.
- Fallbacks: soft eviction policy (LRU-timestamp-aware) for KV entries marked low-reuse; model-variant downgrade route when eviction cannot reclaim enough, with circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: memory_hedge_bytes, hedge_utilization_ratio, forecast_q50/q90/q99, hedge_trigger_reason, preemptive_throttle_count.
- Dashboard: per-GPU hedge vs. free_memory over time, correlation with tail latency and OOM events.

Testing and simulation:
- Build synthetic workload generator (continuous-batch-sim) to replay burst traces from prod (sanitized) and variations (spike, long-tail, multi-tenant collisions).
- Run offline simulation to model different confidence multipliers and risk budgets; publish tradeoff curves.
- Staging canary: deploy on a 10-GPU pool with shadow-mode hedge advisory (no throttling) for 48h, compare against baseline for OOM reduction and utilization loss.

Implementation plan / tasks:
1) Forecast engine prototype (Jordan) -- 2 spikes.
2) Hedge computation service + in-memory per-GPU ledger (sharded) (Jordan + Mei) -- 3 spikes.
3) Scheduler integration: advisory API + throttling hook (Marcus) -- 2 spikes.
4) KV eviction tagging & low-reuse classifier (Ana) -- 3 spikes.
5) Telemetry + dashboards (SRE/Observability) (Liam) -- 2 spikes.
6) Synthetic load generator + offline sim harness (Jordan) -- 2 spikes.
7) Canary rollout and runbook (Ops) -- 1 spike.

Acceptance criteria:
- Offline sim demonstrates >=80% reduction in OOM frequency for spike traces with <6% average utilization loss.
- Canary run shows fewer recoverable evictions and no regression in median latency.
- Telemetry surfaces hedge metrics and alerts when hedging rate exceeds configured SLO.

Risks and mitigations:
- Over-reserving reduces throughput: tune confidence multiplier via sim and progressively lower in canary.
- Forecasting miscalibration under novel workloads: include decay & fast fallback; allow manual override to disable hedging per-pool.
- Multi-tenant fairness issues: enforce per-tenant risk budgets and audit logs for enforced throttles.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: prototype forecast engine and ledger + sim runs.
- Week 3: scheduler integration and telemetry.
- Week 4: canary (shadow then active throttling) and iterate.
- Post-canary: gradual ramp to broader pools with feature flag and config knobs.

Notes/References:
- Related work: adaptive-safety-band-predictive-kv-prefetch (ENG-517420), dynamic-headroom-orchestrator (ENG-468245). This ticket focuses on probabilistic hedging with forecast integration and scheduler advisories, not full prefetching.

Open decisions:
- Forecast window default: 30s vs 60s. 30s preferred for latency-sensitive apps; will validate.
- Default confidence multiplier: 1.4 (start), tune from sim.
comments: 2026-03-02 Priya: Kickoff complete. Jordan to prototype the quantile forecaster; Ana will prepare KV reuse telemetry feed.
2026-03-04 Jordan: Prototype forecaster implemented (sketch-based). Initial 30s q99 estimates look noisy for micro-bursts; adding exponential smoothing.
2026-03-05 Marcus: Scheduler API design drafted; will expose hedger.advisory(gpu_id)->{reserve_bytes, throttles}. Need feedback from SRE on telemetry volumes.
2026-03-06 Ana: KV low-reuse tagging prototype ready; classifier uses LRU age + recent hit-rate delta. Will add weight to eviction score.
2026-03-07 Liam: Dashboard template created in Grafana. Added hedge_utilization_ratio panel and OOM correlation chart.
2026-03-08 Priya: Updated acceptance criteria after sim results. Moving to In Progress.
